main_result.ordering_contract: The K-guard admission token is now embedded in ADMIT before any score-bearing slot can be prepared; SLOT requires a durable active ADMIT; numerical reporting snapshot is embedded in CLOSE and must not be exposed before CLOSE is durably appended. Reporter state is disposable and replayed from the append-only journal.
main_result.handoff_crash_result: A 33-prefix deterministic handoff stress kept prefixes 1-31 in same-history, quarantined prefix 32, and made prefix 33 the first fresh-confirm row after crash/restart replay. The test covered all ADMIT/SLOT/CLOSE write boundaries at prefixes 31/32/33, with exhaustive byte cuts for the actual prefix-32 handoff frames and structural cuts on both neighbors.
main_result.fault_result: 3020 crash-cut cases and 3011 truncate-then-retry cases passed. Tampered admission token, weight-prefix digest, reporting snapshot, and closed-row summary were rejected even after recomputing the outer frame checksum. Torn tails block the next semantic write, and SLOT cannot be prepared before a durable ADMIT.
main_result.module_binding: The adapter pins the previously validated atomic journal, hybrid reporter, production V3, and corrected K-guard by exact sibling filename and repository blob identity so replay cannot silently change statistical semantics.

measurement_validity_rules: Pre-score admission is a durable operation-order requirement, not a caller-side convention. A prepared but unpersisted ADMIT is speculative and cannot authorize slot launch.
The first K-failing row is in neither numerical-reporting phase and remains quarantined after restart.
A prepared CLOSE snapshot is not durable scientific evidence until the CLOSE frame itself is durably appended/fsynced; report exposure must occur after that acknowledgement.
Reporter caches are never a second source of truth. Recovery replays the journal and rejects persisted token/snapshot mismatches.
A torn final frame must be truncated or quarantined to the last valid checksummed prefix before any retry; appending after unreadable garbage is forbidden.
The adapter does not yet retroactively certify legacy journal rows lacking reporting metadata. Safe migration must not claim pre-score admission for such rows.
The crash harness used a contract-faithful fake handoff reporter to isolate durable-integration semantics; it did not revalidate the bound production V3 mathematics from the predecessor checkpoint.
frontier: Byte-execute the persisted adapter against the exact bound sibling modules in a runtime where those repository files are locally available, repeating the handoff crash suite without the fake reporter substrate.
Add a storage/durable-writer acknowledgement API whose returned capability is the only object accepted by slot launch, removing the remaining caller-discipline boundary around fsync acknowledgement.
Stress residual-alpha fresh-allocation replay and actual production V3 endpoint snapshots across CLOSE-before/after crash and report-exposure boundaries.

Define an explicit reporting epoch/migration rule for a pre-existing durable journal containing legacy ADMIT/SLOT/CLOSE frames without reporting metadata; legacy rows may remain in block reliability state but must not be retroactively imported into the K-guard certificate without a valid pre-score contract.

After the durable protocol is byte-executed with production siblings, resume validation-independent optimization of K_cap/alpha split and compare reporting delay/width against fixed .025/.025 fresh reporting.
exact_next_action: Implement a launch-capability/durable-ack wrapper: append+fsync the enriched ADMIT, return a cryptographically bound launch token only after acknowledgement, require that token for every SLOT preparation, and crash-inject the acknowledgement boundary so an unacked or stale token can never launch a score-bearing slot.
